title: Lifting ordinary Hom comparisons to native Weil structures
statement: Let k₀ be a finite field and l a prime different from ringChar k₀, and let X be a scheme over Spec k₀. Fix a NativeFrobeniusRingedModel A and a twisted action-site presentation P of its site, translation and coefficient ring. Define K from P's action-site modules to native Weil sheaves by restriction P.modules.functor followed by IsoAlgebra.mapOfNatIso of A.comparison. Then internal sheaf Hom followed by K is naturally isomorphic to native ihomBifunctor after K in both arguments. Neither existence of A or P nor equivalence of K is asserted by this Hom compatibility lemma.

source.place: Internal-Hom comparison and naturality of evaluation paragraph; underived small-site and fixed-pair parts of the native ringed presentation.

proof.text: For ordinary modules M,N with invertible structure maps tM,tN, expand native ihom_obj_str for their transported structures c_M followed by E(tM) and c_N followed by E(tN). Naturality of precomposition commutes it with postcomposition. Apply A.hom_frobenius to the resulting initial four arrows and A.hom_naturality to the two remaining action arrows. This proves ordinary_hom_action.

For action-site modules take the underlying isomorphism E(P.hom) followed by A.hom. Naturality of c, P.hom_action, and ordinary_hom_action show that it intertwines the native structure maps. Lift this actual isomorphism by Algebra.isoMk and ObjectProperty.isoMk. P.hom_naturality and A.hom_naturality give the bifunctor naturality square; assemble the components with NatIso.ofComponents.

theorem native_action_site_hom_comparison
    {k₀ : Type u} [Field k₀] [Finite k₀] {l : ℕ} [Fact l.Prime]
    [Fact (ringChar k₀ ≠ l)] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))]
    (A : NativeFrobeniusRingedModel k₀ l X)
    (P : Presentation A.J A.s A.R A.a) :
    letI := P.category
    Nonempty
      (Functor.uncurry.obj (SheafOfModules.homFunctor (R := P.coefficient)) ⋙ A.toWeil P ≅
        ((A.toWeil P).op.prod (A.toWeil P)) ⋙
          Functor.uncurry.obj (ihomBifunctor k₀ l X))
